items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about Cannonball Adderley and Porter Kilburn regarding Benny Carter, but does not mention a personal interaction with Benny Carter himself.

ctx.x: He was a teacher for a long time. He tells a marvelous story about Benny Carter coming through Florida, and he sent word for Benny to come over to where he was playing, you know? So he looked up and this fellow walked in and sit down at the table right under and everything, had a case with him. Ordered something to drink and was sitting there and listening. And finally he reached and pulled out his alto and put it together, and come up on stage and he says, “Benny couldn’t come but he sent me,” Porter Kilburn. He…
It was a beautiful era. And I’m very happy that we survived it.

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So Benny Carter made four arrangements for us and he came down to rehearsal and we were delighted.

ctx.x: Milt, really this is going to be really a This Is Your Life kind of interview. I‟ve talked to you on many occasions and you‟ve shared a lot of your memories with me but I‟d really like to go back and do something we haven‟t done. First of all let‟s talk about your childhood. We‟ll start with your childhood. Do you remember your grandparents?

Yeah, both my grandmothers. I remember both of my grandmothers. In fact my mother‟s mother was born a slave. She was born a slave of Joe Davis, Jefferson Davis‟ father. He was president of the South. After the Emancipation Proclamation she took the name of the overseer, which was Carter. So her name was Henry Lettie Carter. After the Emancipation she married a man named Matt Robinson so her last name was Henry Lettie Carter Robinson. This man had a horse and a buggy. He was a hack man. He had what you call a…
Why did they lose so many?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Milt Hinton quoted Benny Carter; INTERVIEWEE confirms being a member of the credit union but does not describe a personal relationship with Hinton.

ctx.x: Very good. Now, two more things. The brief one first. In the Time Life records recreation of the Swing Era, in a book they published, Milt Hinton is quoted as saying that "People don't know this, but Benny -- referring to you -- is responsible for the Musicians Credit Union. It's very hard for musicians to get loans, because they have nothing to give a bank as collateral. Benny confidently went to Local 802 and got them to set up a credit union, and he put in the first $18,000. That was 5 or 6 years ago -- and…
